subject: Energy
title: Hydrogen for Shipping
description: A short lesson to help you apply Hydrogen for Shipping.

hook.text: Global shipping produces 3% of CO₂ emissions—massive container ships burn the dirtiest fuel oil available.

buildup.text: Batteries are too heavy for ocean voyages—a container ship crossing the Pacific needs energy equal to thousands of EVs.

discovery.text: Ammonia (NH₃), made from green hydrogen, can fuel ship engines—it's liquid at mild pressure, easy to store onboard.

twist.text: Ammonia is toxic and corrosive—handling it safely at ports and on ships requires major infrastructure upgrades.

climax.text: Maersk ordered methanol-powered ships instead—the shipping industry is split on which green fuel will win.

punchline.text: Too big for batteries—ships need green fuels like ammonia.

quiz.question: Why can't batteries power ocean-going container ships?
options: Too heavy for the energy needed
